Sure.

For example, imagine I subscribed to /v/gopro and I like to see all hot stuff get submitted to /v/gopro in my frontpage (that's why I subscribe to that certain subverse right?). Well, current algorithm don't allow /v/gopro subscribers to see new stuff which submitted to /v/gopro today in frontpage, since old stuff still on the top of the subverse (with few votes).

This change can fix this problem: After 24 hours from submission, the priority of post go down and new post get submitted shows in subverse hot page top (according to ratio of vote and time it get submitted). This way subscribers are able to see new content in their Voat frontpage feed.

I think this is the problem that users went off from Voat (users didn't see new posts even they are subscribed to lot of interesting subverse that share stuff daily or once in 2 days).

As a result of this non working algorithm, users didn't see the post in frontpage feed and new posts didn't get any votes. And therefore that subverse die in few days...

Reddit did their job very good on this algorithm and it works very well. And that's why people keep seeing new post and vote it up in Reddit.

  1. Subreddit mod creates an account on voat.
  2. That voat account is "linked" to their reddit account.
  3. They begin the process by typing in their subreddit and clicking a few buttons or whatever.
  4. They post on their subreddit to alert users of the migration. They encourage their users to sign up on voat and link their accounts just as they did.
  5. The mod is given some kind of migration stats that let them know how many users have signed up, etc.
  6. When they think enough people have signed up they lock their subreddit and begin the migration.
  7. The program copies the subreddit's posts over to voat and uses the linked user account to post them if available. If not available it uses a special singular dedicated account that they are posted under. The original poster is perhaps mentioned somewhere.
  8. Comments are copied as well using the same process.
